title: autotune: default batching/caching heuristics + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: reduce unit cost and make safe defaults for new and existing customers by automatically recommending batching and caching defaults, applying model quantization profiles where appropriate, and exposing unit-economics tooling to operators. This PR implements a conservative autotune flow: 1) sample workload traces and derive batch_size and batching windows using percentile latency budget heuristics; 2) enable KV/prefix caching defaults for request patterns above threshold; 3) introduce quantization profile metadata for model variants and a safe rollout path; 4) add a unit-economics dashboard + CLI to estimate per-token cost under different config choices. Changes include runtime heuristics, a new autotune controller, CLI tooling, and documentation. Checklist: - [x] Implement autotune controller + config API - [x] Add batching window and batch_size heuristics with unit tests - [x] Integrate prefix/KV cache toggle and thresholds - [x] Add quantization profile metadata and selection logic - [x] Unit-econ tooling (dashboard + CLI) with sample metrics - [x] End-to-end e2e test against perf-canary harness - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Add rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback Strategy and rollout: conservative opt-in default for existing customers, opt-out for Dedicated customers via policy, canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 48h, automatic rollback on latency regression >5p95 or quality regression detected by evals. Metrics collected: p50/p95 latency, tokens/second, cost-per-1M-tokens, request hit-rate for caching. Related: ENG-1245 (autotune roadmap), ENG-1301 (quant profiles), SUP-402 (customers requesting cheaper defaults).
